By test step

✓pass✕new failure●known failure⚠job failed in setup⊘skipped: an earlier step failed–not run

A step that shows ⊘ or – for several pushes is a blind spot: the GPU's verdict cannot see it.

New failures: tests that passed on the previous push and fail now

A test is new when it failed on this push and passed on the previous push that ran its step on the same GPU. Pushes where the step was skipped or hit a setup failure do not count. On the step's next result it moves to Known, keeping the push it first failed at. The last column checks the scheduled run of the same commit: a failure it reproduces is real, one it does not is a flake candidate.

Setup failures

A setup failure leaves no test result for that job, so the next push compares against the last push that has one.

Perf events from the TLX ops bench, last two nights

Pull requests

Directional signal, earlierOwner: PR author
A red PR is the PR author's to fix. These results do not count toward main's health. Two exceptions: a failure that also fails on main is not the author's (tagged fails on main), and a setup failure is CI's (tagged setup: CI, counted on the Operations tab).

Operations

Is CI itself healthy, and what does it cost?Owner: CI maintainers

Smart trigger: what the select job ran, last 7 days

PR and push runs should run only the GPUs their changed paths touch, and skip the build when none are touched. Scheduled and manual runs should run every GPU. A fallback means the changed paths were unavailable, so every suite ran.
